arxiv-1510-01183.title: Robinson–Trautman solution with nonlinear electrodynamics
arxiv-1510-01183.creator: T. Tahamtan e1,addr1, O. Svítek e2,addr1
arxiv-1510-01183.description: A 2015 arXiv research paper by T. Tahamtan e1,addr1, O. Svítek e2,addr1. Explicit Robinson–Trautman solutions with electromagnetic field satisfying nonlinear field equations are derived and analyzed. The solutions are generated from the spherically symmetric ones. In all studied cases the electromagnetic field singularity is removed while the gravitational one persists.

Keywords: Inverse-strongly monotone mapping; Strongly monotone mapping;
arxiv-1802-02726.creator: Ravi P. Agarwal 1 , Ebrahim Soori ∗,2 , Donal O’Regan 3
arxiv-1802-02726.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Ravi P. Agarwal 1 , Ebrahim Soori ∗,2 , Donal O’Regan 3. In this paper, a simple proof is presented for the Convergence of the algorithms for the class of relaxed ( u , v ) (u,v) -cocoercive mappings and α \alpha -inverse strongly monotone mappings. Based on α \alpha -expansive maps, for example, a simple proof of the convergence of the recent iterative algorithms by relaxed ( u , v ) (u,v) -cocoercive mappings due to Kumam-Jaiboon is provided.

arxiv-2109-02202.title: Fairness via AI: Bias Reduction in Medical Information
arxiv-2109-02202.creator: Shiri Dori-Hacohen, Roberto Montenegro, Fabricio Murai, Scott A. Hale, Keen Sung, Michela Blain, Jennifer Edwards-Johnson
arxiv-2109-02202.description: Abstract 1 Introduction Most Fairness in AI research focuses on exposing biases in AI systems. A broader lens on fairness reveals that AI can serve a greater aspiration: rooting out societal inequities from their source. Specifically, we focus on inequities in health information, and aim to reduce bias in that domain using AI.

arxiv-2111-01518.title: Multiple recurrence and convergence without commutativity Thanks: The first author was supported by the Research Grant - ELIDEK HFRI-FM17-1684.
arxiv-2111-01518.creator: Nikos Frantzikinakis, Bernard Host
arxiv-2111-01518.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Nikos Frantzikinakis, Bernard Host. We establish multiple recurrence and convergence results for pairs of zero entropy measure preserving transformations that do not satisfy any commutativity assumptions. Our results cover the case where the iterates of the two transformations are n n and n k n^{k} respectively, where k ≥ 2 k\geq 2 , and the case k = 1 k=1 remains an open problem.

arxiv-2208-03492.title: Pitching strategy evaluation via stratified analysis using propensity score
arxiv-2208-03492.creator: Hiroshi Nakahara, Kazuya Takeda, *
arxiv-2208-03492.description: Abstract Recent measurement technologies enable us to analyze baseball at higher levels. There are, however, still many unclear points around the pitching strategy. The two elements make it difficult to measure the effect of pitching strategy. First, most public datasets do not include location data where the catcher demands a ball, which is essential information to obtain the battery’s intent.

arxiv-2405-10929.title: Quantifying risk of a noise-induced AMOC collapse from northern and tropical Atlantic Ocean variability
arxiv-2405-10929.creator: R Chapman, P Ashwin, J Baker, R A Wood
arxiv-2405-10929.description: Abstract The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) exerts a major influence on global climate. There is much debate about whether the current strong AMOC may collapse as a result of anthropogenic forcing and/or internal variability. Increasing the noise in simple salt-advection models can change the apparent AMOC tipping threshold.

pmc-10571005.title: Expanding the Potential of Identical Location Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy for Gas Evolving Reactions: Stability of Rhenium Molybdenum Disulfide Nanocatalysts for Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
pmc-10571005.creator: Miquel Vega-Paredes, Christina Scheu, Raquel Aymerich-Armengol
pmc-10571005.description: Identical location (scanning) transmission electron microscopy provides valuable insights into the mechanisms of the activity and degradation of nanocatalysts during electrochemical reactions. However, the technique suffers from limitations that hinder its widespread use for nanocatalysts of gas evolving reactions, e.g., the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER).

pmc-11514175.title: RACK1 contributes to the upregulation of embryonic genes in a model of cardiac hypertrophy
pmc-11514175.creator: Marcello Ceci, Davide Bonvissuto, Flavia Papetti, Federica Silvestri, Claudio Sette, Elisabetta Catalani, Davide Cervia, Rosalba Gornati, Nicla Romano
pmc-11514175.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Receptors for activated C kinases (RACKs) have been shown to coordinate PKC-mediated hypertrophic signalling in mice. However, little information is available on its participation in embryonic gene expression. This study investigated the involvement of RACK1 in the expression of embryonic genes in a zebrafish (ZF) ex vivo heart culture model by using phenylephrine (PE) or a growth factors cocktail (GFs) as a prohypertrophic/regeneration stimulus.

pmc-12482792.title: A case of juvenile chronic encapsulated intracerebral hematoma requiring differential diagnosis, successfully treated with craniotomy and hematoma evacuation
pmc-12482792.creator: Yodai Kikuchi, Shogo Dofuku, Rika Nakamura, Ken Kazama, Hideaki Imai
pmc-12482792.description: Background: Chronic encapsulated intracerebral hematoma (CEIH) is a rare condition with an unclear pathogenesis. Moreover, no consensus has been established regarding its treatment. Here, we report a case of juvenile subcortical CEIH successfully treated with complete resection, including the capsule.

pmc-12555625.title: The impact of chosen socio-demographic determinants on average age at death of Roma in Slovenia
pmc-12555625.creator: T Krajnc Nikolic, K Rostohar, M Ranfl
pmc-12555625.description: The average life expectancy of Roma in Slovenia is shorter than of non-Roma population. We were interested in exploring the impact of selected social-education and demographic-gender factors on the average age at death of Roma, compared to non-Roma population. The population of Roma settlements was selected from the Slovenian Population Register.

pmc-12734213.title: Differences in Maternal and Neonatal Outcomes Between Pregnancies Following Intrauterine Insemination (IUI) and In Vitro Fertilization (IVF): A Review
pmc-12734213.creator: Panagiotis Cherouveim, Esra Cetin, Shagun Tuli, Taylor Lombard, Youssef Youssef, Gaby Moawad, Jean Marc Ayoubi, Anis Feki, Andrea Tinelli
pmc-12734213.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Pregnancies following Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) are associated with increased risk for adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. However, it is not clear if these associations are derived from infertility or fertility treatment itself. The goal of this review is to investigate if there are differences in maternal and neonatal outcomes between pregnancies conceived through either intrauterine insemination (IUI) or in vitro fertilization (IVF) to obtain an estimate of the effect of the fertility treatment.

pmc-13299997.title: Outcomes of Curative Esophagectomy in Octogenarians vs. Non-Octogenarians with Esophageal Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13299997.creator: Liyang Xiao, Kai Siang Chan, Isaac Chan, Aung Myint Oo
pmc-13299997.description: Background: Esophageal cancer (EC) poses a growing global challenge in the context of an ageing population. Evidence on the role of curative esophagectomy in octogenarians is limited. This study aims to compare the long-term survival and post-operative mortality and morbidity in octogenarians undergoing curative esophagectomy for EC with those in non-octogenarians.

pmc-13439885.title: Relationship between first-aid literacy, coping style, family functioning and mental health of caregivers of children with asthma
pmc-13439885.creator: Mingjing Fu, Xiujie Sun, Yaoyao Zhang, Kun Chi, Shanshan Huan, Zihan Gao, Huan Han, Wenjing Wang, Xiangdi Dong
pmc-13439885.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe rising prevalence of childhood bronchial asthma imposes a substantial economic burden and threatens the mental health of affected families, worldwide. Although multiple factors influence caregivers’ psychological wellbeing, systematic investigations in this area are still lacking. Hence, this study aimed to explore the relationship between first-aid literacy, coping style, family functioning, and the mental health of caregivers of children with asthma.MethodsThis cross-sectional descriptive study included 337 children with asthma and their parents.

pmc-13643565.title: Pectus Excavatum
pmc-13643565.creator: Krishnaswamy Chandrasekaran, Farouk Mookadam
pmc-13643565.description: Corresponding Author Pectus excavatum (PE) is usually not considered causative in adults presenting with cardiopulmonary symptoms despite a thorough cardiopulmonary evaluation by cardiologists and pulmonologists for disabling cardiopulmonary symptoms.1,2 Kragten et al1 developed a score for evaluating symptoms, the symptomatic pectus excavatum in seniors (SPES) score, and the magnitude of pectus compression, the pectus evaluation index score (PEI).
